Community

Buittle Parish Community Council

Our community council is consulted by law on issues that matter to our community — and it has to listen to us on issues important to us.

Our community council receives and can comment on planning and licensing applications relevant to the Buittle Parish Community Council boundary. Palnackie sits within the area of Buittle Parish.

The meeting schedule, contact details and the Buittle Parish Boundary Map can be found on the Dumfries and Galloway Council website:

Buittle Parish Community Council — Dumfries & Galloway Council

Minutes of recent Buittle Parish Community Council meetings are available in the village shop.

Becoming a councillor

Community councils are run entirely by volunteers — local residents aged 16 and above who care about where they live. No experience, qualifications, or public speaking confidence is needed.

What the role actually involves

Most people assume it’s more demanding than it is.

Meetings happen roughly once a quarter, usually on a weekday evening in the village hall. Most run for 60–90 minutes.

Between meetings, you’ll spend around 20–30 minutes reading meeting papers sent a few days beforehand. Occasionally there are site visits or community events to attend.

Total time commitment: roughly 2–4 hours a month for an ordinary member. Some councillors take on specific responsibilities (treasurer, secretary, planning liaison) — but that’s optional and roles are shared.

What you don’t need

  • Any prior experience of councils or committees
  • Legal, planning, or financial expertise
  • Any particular qualifications

What helps

  • Caring about Palnackie and wanting to see it thrive
  • Basic reliability — turning up to meetings and reading the papers
  • Being willing to listen to different views

Why it matters

Decisions get made whether or not local people are at the table. The community council is where Palnackie residents can influence planning decisions, road and infrastructure issues, local services, and what gets funded. A healthy, well-represented council means the village has a stronger voice with Dumfries & Galloway Council and other bodies.

Interested?

You’re welcome to come along to a meeting as a visitor first — no commitment required. New members are supported by existing councillors from day one.

To find out more, email community-council@palnackie.com or speak to any existing councillor in the village.
